title: In one LINK monkey, a GRU gained 0.036 R^2 per doubling of pretraining sessions and data, and 0.017 from 16 to 64, with a budget that grew with pool size; a fixed budget gave at least as large a gain
abstract: Campaign branch D, leaf D1, confirmatory follow-up (revision 1). Question: an earlier campaign paper found that a small GRU decoder gained 0.030 R^2 per doubling of pretraining sessions on LINK (DANDI 001201), but it used a fixed 3000-step budget for every pool size, and its reviewers found that the gain above 16 sessions depended on that budget. We retested on 20 test days (2021-08-31 to 2021-10-27) that the earlier paper did not use; no day overlaps. Setup: one rhesus monkey, 96 Utah-array channels, spike-band power, 2-DoF finger velocity, 20 labelled calibration trials per new day, a 64-session pool, 4 seeds (4 distinct pools for N <= 16, 2 at N = 32, 1 at N = 64). The budget rule, steps = max(3000, 375 x N), was chosen on separate discovery days and preregistered before any confirmatory fit (self-attested hash and time). Because of the 3000-step floor, the budget comparison concerns N >= 16. Results: with the growing budget, the GRU gained +0.036 [0.026, 0.046] R^2 per doubling over N = 1 to 64 and +0.017 [0.010, 0.025] from 16 to 64 (preregistered two-level bootstrap; both met the thresholds 0.02 and 0.01; a post hoc seed-level t interval gives [0.018, 0.053] and [0.009, 0.026]). The fixed 3000-step budget gave a large-N gain at least as large (+0.022 [0.016, 0.029]); the predicted benefit of the growing budget did not occur (difference -0.005 [-0.010, +0.001]). Doubling the budget again at N = 64 (seed 0; 48000 vs 24000 steps) changed R^2 by +0.000 [-0.009, +0.010]. Ridge gained +0.004 per doubling. Thus the earlier session-scaling result is not an artefact of its fixed budget in these data. A post hoc equal-data control found no gain from more sessions at a fixed total number of trials, so the gain tracks the amount of pretraining data, not session diversity. Limitations: one animal, offline task, dependent test days, one pool at N = 64, mostly center-out days, one budget rule and one small architecture.

display.caption: a: held-out R^2 against pretraining sessions for the GRU with a growing budget (arm P), with a fixed 3000-step budget (arm F), and for ridge. b: gain per doubling with 95% CIs over days and seeds.

citations.reason: We retest its GRU session-scaling claim with a training budget that grows with pool size, on non-overlapping LINK days. The claim held (b = +0.036, 16-64 gain = +0.017), and the fixed 3000-step budget did not limit the gain at N = 64. A post hoc equal-data control indicates that the gain tracks the amount of pretraining data rather than session diversity. We read its README for the setup and wrote new code.
The earlier linear-decoder campaign paper on LINK; our ridge session slopes agree with it.
LINK dataset paper (Temmar et al., NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks).
BrainGate 20-year Utah-array study (Hahn et al. 2026); campaign context. Its data were not used here.
